cases.question: Current AX-17 renal guidance in Germany?
cases.answer:
The current renal guidance for AX-17 in Germany specifies: Normal (eGFR >=90): starting dose 50 mg OD, maximum 100 mg/day [E2]. Mild (eGFR 60-89): starting dose 50 mg OD, maximum 100 mg/day [E2]. Moderate (eGFR 30-59): starting dose 25 mg OD, maximum 50 mg/day, monitoring recheck 2-4 weeks [E2]. Severe (eGFR 15-29): starting dose specialist review, maximum 25 mg/day [E2].

cases.question: German AX-17 guidance before latest revision?
cases.answer:
Part 1
Historical view: documents in effect on 2026-09-14.

The superseded German AX-17 guidance (in effect 2025-02-03 to 2026-09-15) [E1] stated the following historical starting doses for renal impairment: 50 mg OD for normal [E1], 50 mg OD for mild [E1], 50 mg OD for moderate [E1], and not recommended for severe [E1].

Sources
[E1] DE-AX17-LBL-038 · DE AX17 Superseded Label v3.8 · SUPERSEDED · effective 2025-02-03 · p.6, Historical renal dosing
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/DE_AX17_Superseded_Label_v3.8.pdf#page=6

Current version: DE-AX17-LBL-042 (DE AX17 Current Label v4.2), in effect since 2026-09-15. Ask for the current guidance to see it.

Part 2
The current German AX-17 guidance includes a temporary hepatic monitoring enhancement requiring baseline hepatic laboratory values with repeat testing between Day 14 and Day 21 [E1]. Hepatic monitoring thresholds are: ALT/AST >3x ULN (medical review), bilirubin >2x ULN (urgent review), and mild isolated change below trigger (repeat test) [E2]. Renal dose modifications (Table 3) are: Normal (eGFR >=90): starting dose 50 mg OD, maximum 100 mg/day, routine monitoring [E4]; Mild (eGFR 60-89): starting dose 50 mg OD, maximum 100 mg/day, routine monitoring [E4]; Moderate (eGFR 30-59): starting dose 25 mg OD, maximum 50 mg/day, monitoring recheck 2-4 weeks [E4]; Severe (eGFR 15-29): specialist review, maximum 25 mg/day, enhanced monitoring [E4].

cases.question: What does SB-AX17-2026-09 require?
cases.answer:
SB-AX17-2026-09 requires baseline hepatic laboratory values with repeat testing between Day 14 and Day 21 [E1]. For ALT/AST >3x ULN, medical review is required [E2]. For Bilirubin >2x ULN, urgent review is required [E2]. For mild isolated changes below the trigger, a repeat test is required [E2]. cases.question: Compare AE evidence in HN-204 and HN-311.
cases.answer:
In HN-204, treatment-emergent adverse events for AX-17 range from 12.7% for nausea to 19.1% for transaminase elevation, versus control rates of 6.0% to 9.0% [E1]. The highest treatment % in HN-204 is transaminase elevation at 19.1 [E4]. In HN-311, treatment-emergent adverse events for AX-17 range from 11.8% for nausea to 17.7% for transaminase elevation, versus control rates of 6.0% to 9.0% [E2]. The highest treatment % in HN-311 is transaminase elevation at 17.7 [E4]. All treatment percentage differences (HN-311 minus HN-204) lie between -1.4 points and -0.9 points [E4], and control percentage differences are +0.0 points [E4].

Sources
[E1] HN-204 · HN-204 Clinical Study v1.0 · APPROVED · effective 2025-06-12 · p.11, Table 14
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/HN-204_Clinical_Study.pdf#page=11
[E2] HN-311 · HN-311 Clinical Study v1.0 · APPROVED · effective 2026-01-18 · p.11, Table 14
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/HN-311_Clinical_Study.pdf#page=11
[E4] computed by code from [E3] (differences and highest values; not document text)

Descriptive comparison across separate studies, not a head-to-head result.
